targets.text: A Govee lamp is a culture-rules actor any workflow can drive, and a daily wake-up workflow fades it in at 06:20
a lamp_* step run from culture-rules changes the real H6076 lamp, seen in govee stats with source rules

The lamp is reached through a culture-rules runner actor whose params.commands registry (culture_rules/actors/code.py) holds govee-cli's named lamp commands (lamp_on, lamp_off, lamp_brightness, lamp_color, lamp_temp, lamp_scene, lamp_fade_on, lamp_fade_off), each argv the absolute govee path ending --source rules --apply --json; govee-cli generates the definition with 'govee rules actor' (govee-cli docs/culture-rules/README.md)
the actor's commands are exactly what 'govee rules actor' prints on spark, every argv[0] absolute and no argv a shell or interpreter, so inline_guard admits all 8

govee-cli owns the lamp command list and the actor definition; culture-rules commits no govee actor JSON (the argv path is per machine, govee-cli README) and no wake-up bundle; schedules live in culture-rules' store, never in govee-cli
git diff of the delivery holds no govee actor JSON and no wake-up workflow or rule in either repo; the actor, workflow and rule exist only in the live store

The wake-up is a schedule rule (stdlib cron, IANA tz Asia/Jerusalem) at 06:20 daily that starts a workflow whose step calls the lamp actor's fade-in command; the step is placed on the machine the lamp's runner lives on (spark)
the rule's trigger is kind schedule with cron 20 6 * * * and tz Asia/Jerusalem, and its workflow step is placed on spark where the runner and the lamp's LAN are
The operator at home on spark, and any culture-rules workflow author who wants a lamp as a step
the operator, not a mesh agent, enables the wake-up rule; any workflow author can add a lamp step without touching govee-cli
The lamp is one enabled actor in the Actors tab; any workflow calls lamp_* commands by name with typed args, and a schedule rule fades the lamp in each morning at 06:20 Asia/Jerusalem
culture-rules actors references on the lamp actor lists the wake-up workflow, and the actor is enabled on machine spark
govee-cli can drive the lamp from its CLI, web console and MCP, but no culture-rules actor exists for it, so no rule or workflow can touch the lamp
before this delivery no culture-rules actor had a govee argv (checked live with actors list once a token is set)
Lights become a reusable output of the mesh (CI red, wake-up, bedtime) by configuration alone, with govee-cli keeping ownership of how the lamp is spoken to
a second flow can use the lamp with only a new workflow step, no new actor and no code
On 1 morning after enabling, the run at 06:20 Asia/Jerusalem succeeds within 60 s of the scheduled time, govee's event log shows the fade with source rules, and the lamp ends on
the first morning's run record and govee stats (source rules) are read back and attached as evidence, not assumed

tasks.summary: Reinstall govee on spark from govee-cli main
acceptance_criteria: govee rules actor --json on spark exits 0 and prints a runner actor with 8 commands (o9)
govee --version on spark matches pyproject.toml on govee-cli origin/main
tasks.instruction: Operator shell step on spark: uv tool install --force --from git+https://github.com/agentculture/govee-cli@main govee-cli (or from a fresh checkout of origin/main; the local main is 77 commits behind). Check with command -v govee and govee rules actor --json. Ask before running.

tasks.summary: Run govee serve always-on on spark with a culture-rules client token
acceptance_criteria: systemctl --user is-enabled govee-serve and is-active govee-serve both succeed, and it is still active after systemctl --user restart govee-serve (o5)
govee token list shows a token named culture-rules saved to the client-token file (o6)
tasks.instruction: Install govee-cli's docs/systemd/govee-serve.service as a user unit (linger is already yes for spark), daemon-reload, enable --now. Then govee token new --name culture-rules --save as user spark, the same user culture-rules-node.service runs as. GOVEE_API_KEY stays in serve's env file only. Ask before starting the unit.

tasks.summary: Import the lamp runner actor into the live store and prove one step drives the lamp
acceptance_criteria: before the import, culture-rules actors list --json holds no actor with a govee argv (h9)
culture-rules actors show of the new actor has params.commands equal to govee rules actor --json output: 8 commands, absolute argv[0], each ending --source rules --apply --json (o2)
a scratch workflow run with one lamp_color step on spark succeeds (no InlineCommandDenied) and govee events shows the change with source rules (o1, o3)
a lamp_fade_on step with seconds 600 returns in under 10 s while govee light fade-status shows the fade running (o5)
tasks.instruction: Generate with govee rules actor --bin "$(command -v govee)" --machine spark into the scratchpad, read it, then culture-rules actors create --body @file (dry run), then --apply. Needs CULTURE_RULES_TOKEN injected from grant (hidden admin token, inject only). The scratch workflow is live only and is deleted after; nothing is committed.

culture-rules actors references on the lamp actor lists the wake-up workflow, and the actor is enabled on spark (o10)
the wake-up workflow adds no actor and no code: it reuses the t3 actor (h10)
the rule is created disabled; the operator enables it (h7)

risks.text: If govee serve is down at 06:20 the runner falls back to direct LAN, so a long fade holds the step for its whole length (timeout 3660 s) instead of failing fast
After a fade-out the lamp rests at brightness 1; how lamp_fade_on behaves from that state is a wake-up detail for the workflow config, outside this plan

The runner starts commands with only PATH and LANG; under env -i with exactly those govee found its client token via the passwd home and read the lamp through serve (2026-10-30); a run under the node itself is still t3's
risks.resolution: under the node itself (runs on 2026-10-30) govee found its token and routed through serve; resolved

risks.text: lamp_fade_on fades to the lamp's last level, and after a fade-out that level is 1 (seen live: target brightness 1); a wake-up needs a fade to a chosen brightness, but govee rules actor's lamp_brightness has no seconds param although govee light brightness takes --fade. The command list is govee-cli's (boundary c5)
risks.resolution: deviation d1: govee-cli adds light on --brightness and lamp_fade_on_to {pct, seconds}; the actor is regenerated and updated
